newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Wednesday, driven lower by profit-taking and a weak bond market.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average lost 52.98 points to 7,172.34. In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 13-9 on volume of 271 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up 3.03 points to 1,331.33.

The blue-chip Dow index has gained nearly 250 points since last Friday, partly on hopes that a balanced budget agreement would keep the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates again later this month.
"We are seeing normal profit-taking in the Dow stocks which have been up significantly," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

"We have decent activity in Nasdaq, good volume and new highs still lead new lows on the Big Board," he said. "This kind of profit-taking is normal after the spectacular run we've been having. The bottom line is that despite the fact that we are down, the bullish tenor continues."
The 30-year Treasury bond fell 18/32, raising its yield to 6.94 percent from 6.89 percent at Tuesday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
"Stocks are taking their cue from bonds. If the bond market can't rally any more, we will have problems," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

"Also, the dollar has been easier over the last few days, and it seems as though central banks want to put a lid on it. Not let it rise any further. If that is the case, it will diminish the flow of foreign funds into dollar instruments."
Peter Cardillo, chief investment strategist at Westfalia Investments said the market was having a correction.

"This is healthy for the stock market," he said. "Any pullback will be shallow. Over the next week or so, we'll be heading back down to 7,000 level on the Dow which will make for a good buying opportunity."
The stock of most major oil companies were higher, bucking a lower market trend.

Atlantic Richfield Co. added 1-1/2 to 145-1/2 after it announced that reserves at its Alpine field in Alaska were higher than originally forecast. Anadarko Petroleum Corp., also a partner in the Alpine field, rose 1-3/8 to 59.
Chevron Corp. was up 1/4 to 69-3/4, Mobil Corp. gained 1/2 to 132-1/4 and Texaco Inc. 3/4 to 108-3/8.
